lead: FIFA and CAF ordered Nigeria's football federation to suspend its election process while they assess the leadership crisis. Six trafficked children died in captivity in Oyo as police rescued 17 others, and a three-storey building collapsed in Abuja hours after officials sealed it. Peter Obi's convoy was reportedly blocked in Benue, petrol imports rose almost elevenfold in the second quarter, and security agencies said 1,487 terrorists were killed in July and August.

items.h: FIFA and CAF suspend NFF election process
items.s: FIFA and the Confederation of African Football ordered Nigeria's football federation to halt its electoral process immediately and will send a joint mission to Abuja to assess the leadership crisis. The elective congress had been set for 27 September in Lafia.

items.h: Six trafficked children die in captivity as police rescue 17 in Oyo
items.s: Oyo police said six children taken by a suspected child-trafficking ring died in captivity, while 17 were rescued and seven suspects arrested. One suspect allegedly confessed to selling her own newborn twins for N300,000.

items.h: Abuja building collapses hours after it was sealed
items.s: A three-storey commercial building in Wuse Zone 4 collapsed on Monday evening, hours after FCT development control officials sealed it and told occupants to leave.

items.h: Obi's convoy reportedly blocked in Benue
items.s: NDC figures condemned a reported attack and blockade of presidential candidate Peter Obi's convoy in Benue State and asked the police and DSS chiefs to call governors to order.

items.h: ONSA says 1,487 terrorists killed in two months
items.s: The Office of the National Security Adviser said security operations in July and August killed 1,487 terrorists, citing better coordination and intelligence.

items.h: Petrol import bill jumps 989% to N952bn in second quarter
items.s: Nigeria spent N952.15 billion on petrol imports in the second quarter of 2026, up from N87.40 billion in the first quarter.

items.h: Dangote refinery aims for 10 million investors in N2.15trn IPO
items.s: The Dangote refinery said its initial public offering, valued at about N2.15 trillion or $1.6 billion, targets up to 10 million Nigerian subscribers.

items.h: INEC to launch real-time election readiness tracker
items.s: INEC said it will use a live tracker to monitor preparations for the 2027 elections in all 36 states and the FCT.

items.h: Tinubu mourns State House media official who died in Kano
items.s: President Tinubu mourned Peter Onwubuariri, an assistant director of media at the Presidential Villa and former News Agency of Nigeria journalist, who died in Kano aged 48.

items.h: Police enforce Lagos judgment in Tinubu land dispute
items.s: Police began enforcing a Lagos High Court judgment in a long-running dispute over 114.476 hectares in Ogombo village, Eti-Osa.

items.h: Gunmen kill three vigilantes in Kaduna
items.s: Three members of the Kaduna State Vigilance Service were killed on the Zuntu-Zaria road in Kubau at about 12.20am on Monday as they went off duty.

items.h: Bandits kill vigilante and abduct resident in Kano village
items.s: Bandits attacked Dakwara village in Gwarzo early on Tuesday, killing a vigilante and kidnapping a resident, the village head said.

items.h: Troops rescue 12 civilians in Zamfara
items.s: Operation Fansan Yamma rescued 12 people during operations in Kaura Namoda and Tsafe.

items.h: Katsina governor presents N828.6bn 2027 budget
items.s: Governor Dikko Radda sent a N828.64 billion budget for 2027 to the Katsina Assembly, 7.71 per cent less than the approved 2026 budget.

items.h: Super Eagles to play Russia in October friendly
items.s: The NFF confirmed a friendly against Russia, currently banned by FIFA, in Nizhny Novgorod on 6 October.

items.h: Falconets lose 2-0 to Spain in World Cup opener
items.s: Nigeria's under-20 women lost 2-0 to Spain in Sosnowiec, Poland, at the start of their FIFA U20 Women's World Cup campaign.

items.h: Eguavoen named interim Super Falcons coach
items.s: Augustine Eguavoen will lead the Super Falcons against Comoros in the 2028 Olympic qualifiers while the NFF searches for a permanent coach.

items.h: CBN makes terrorism financing a supervisory priority
items.s: The Central Bank said it has raised terrorism financing to a current supervisory priority to protect banks from abuse.

items.h: Six Nigerian firms make FTSE Frontier 50 index
items.s: FirstHoldCo, Zenith, GTCO, Dangote Cement, Aradel and MTN Nigeria are the only Nigerian companies in FTSE Russell's Frontier 50 Index.

items.h: FG begins exclusive talks with APM Terminals on Badagry port
items.s: The Federal Government started exclusive negotiations with APM Terminals to develop the proposed Badagry deep seaport.

items.h: Grid operator holds hearing on DisCos' market debts
items.s: The Nigerian Independent System Operator concluded a public hearing with distribution companies on their unpaid obligations to the electricity market.

items.h: NMDPRA denies under-remitting gas flare penalties
items.s: The downstream regulator rejected an Auditor-General finding that gas flare penalties had been under-remitted to the gas infrastructure fund.

items.h: Crude nears $100, raising fears of petrol price rise
items.s: Oil approached $100 a barrel on Tuesday, renewing concern about another round of pump price increases in Nigeria.

items.h: Atiku blames Tinubu for foreign investors' exit and heavy borrowing
items.s: Atiku Abubakar said the flight of foreign portfolio investment shows no confidence in the government's economic management, and questioned domestic borrowing despite higher oil prices.

items.h: Fayemi likens Atiku's subsidy pledge to a campaign ploy
items.s: Former Ekiti governor Kayode Fayemi said Atiku Abubakar's proposal to restore the petrol subsidy exploits hardship for votes.

items.h: APC figure asks agencies to probe Atiku allegations
items.s: Former APC national vice chairman Hilliard Eta urged anti-corruption agencies to investigate allegations involving Atiku Abubakar.

items.h: Osun tribunal starts hearing; APC legal team disowns petition
items.s: The Osun governorship tribunal began proceedings on petitions against Governor Ademola Adeleke's re-election, but the APC's legal team in the state disowned the petition filed in the party's name.

items.h: NDC denies illegal payments in candidate selection
items.s: The Nigeria Democratic Congress rejected claims of illegal payments and favouritism in choosing its 2027 candidates.

items.h: Kwara defectors say PDP offers a better platform
items.s: APC members who moved to the PDP in Kwara said the opposition party gives them a better political future.

items.h: Lagos APC opens 2027 mobilisation for Tinubu
items.s: The APC in Lagos said re-electing President Tinubu is in the national interest, and Governor Sanwo-Olu said the party will take no voter for granted.

items.h: Rivers ADC tells Wike intimidation will not win elections
items.s: The ADC in Rivers responded to Wike's claim that its vice-presidential candidate Rotimi Amaechi would be defeated.

items.h: Shettima calls for peaceful, issue-based campaign
items.s: Vice President Kashim Shettima urged APC campaigners to keep their mobilisation peaceful, and said the government is working to cut transport costs.

items.h: Churches back state police to tackle insecurity
items.s: The Christ Church Spiritual Advisory Council, linking the Anglican, Methodist and Presbyterian churches, endorsed state police.

items.h: Plateau sends medical supplies to diphtheria treatment centres
items.s: Governor Caleb Mutfwang ordered drugs and medical supplies sent to facilities treating diphtheria patients.

items.h: ONSA starts multi-agency crisis response drill in Delta
items.s: The Presidential Command and Control Centre began a week-long exercise in Delta to test security agencies' readiness for crises.

items.h: Nigerian scientist wins $100,000 NLNG prize for AI MRI tool
items.s: Mary Brenda Akoda took the $100,000 Nigeria Prize for Science and Innovation for GenScan AI, an artificial intelligence tool that shortens the time needed for MRI scans.

items.h: Oxford names MDCN head Fatima Kyari visiting fellow
items.s: The University of Oxford named Prof. Fatima Kyari, registrar of the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria, its 2026 Aig-Imoukhuede Visiting Fellow.

items.h: Credit guarantee company mobilises N46.95bn in first year
items.s: The National Credit Guarantee Company said it unlocked N46.95 billion in credit for businesses and individuals in its first year.

items.h: Enugu palm firm invests $2.2m in refinery
items.s: United Palm Products began commercial production and is investing $2.2 million in a refinery to process crude palm oil.

items.h: Customs officer dies in Cross River crash
items.s: Etteng Ise, 54, a Customs officer at the Mfum border, died when he lost control of his car avoiding a pothole on the Ikom-Calabar highway.

items.h: Bauchi police arrest seven over Dass clashes
items.s: Bauchi police said seven suspects are in custody over the 4 September clashes in Dass that killed two people.

items.h: Yusuf Alli says Intermediate Games will expose athlete poaching
items.s: Olympian Yusuf Alli said Eko 2026 will show which states invest in grassroots sport and which poach athletes.
